files.lesson.md: --- order: 18 unit: time node: [AC9M8M04 n1, AC9M8M04 n2] title: Time zones summary: "A city with a bigger UTC offset is ahead; a smaller offset is behind. Find the difference between the two offsets, then add or take it away; the day changes when you cross midnight. A flight's arrival time is the departure time plus the flight, changed to the local time where it lands." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "You call your cousin in London after school and wake her up at 5 am. A flight from Sydney lands in Los Angeles before it took off. Time zones explain both." connection: overseas-match # data/connections/maths.yml app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8309 url: http://127.0.0.1:8309/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: zones.yml#explain, caption: "9:00 am Monday in Sydney is 6:00 am in Perth, 11:00 pm Sunday in London and 7:00 am in Tokyo." } explainClip: query: { code: "@zones.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "One moment, four clocks" say: "Move Sydney's time, and every city moves with it." clip: - caption: { text: "9 am Monday in Sydney: London is still on Sunday night.", say: "Nine on Monday morning in Sydney. London is still on Sunday night." } - wait: 1200 - caption: { text: "One hour later in Sydney: one hour later everywhere.", say: "One hour later in Sydney is one hour later everywhere." } - click: Make the time in Sydney later - click: Make the time in Sydney later - click: Make the time in Sydney later - click: Make the time in Sydney later - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Sydney 10:00" } - wait: 1500 --- Each place keeps its own clock, set by its **time zone**. A zone is written as its **offset** from UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). This lesson uses the offsets for 4 to 24 October 2026: Sydney UTC+11 (daylight saving, from 4 October 2026 to 4 April 2027; UTC+10 the rest of the year), Perth UTC+8, Tokyo UTC+9, London UTC+1 (its clocks go back on 25 October) and Los Angeles UTC−7 (until 1 November). Outside those dates some of these differences change by an hour, so check again before you plan a real call. These were checked on [timeanddate.com](https://www.timeanddate.com/) for [Sydney](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/change/australia/sydney), [Perth](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zone/australia/perth), [Tokyo](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zone/japan/tokyo), [London](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zone/uk/london) and [Los Angeles](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/pt) ([its clock change](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/change/usa/los-angeles)). The dates move every year. To change a time from one zone to another, find the **difference** between the offsets. A place with a bigger offset is **ahead** (later); a smaller offset is **behind** (earlier). Go by the offsets, not the map: Los Angeles is east of Sydney across the Pacific, but across the International Date Line, so it is 18 hours behind. Add or take away the difference, and change the **day** if you cross midnight. **24-hour time** (21:30, not 9:30 pm) avoids mixing up morning and night. For a flight: add the flight time to the departure time (in the departure zone), then change to the arrival zone. ## Predict: London on Monday morning ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to London's time from Sydney's shows whether they take the difference the right way and change the day." check: type: predict q: "It is 9:00 am Monday in Sydney (UTC+11). What time is it in London (UTC+1)?" options: ["11:00 pm Sunday", "7:00 pm Monday", "7:00 pm Sunday", "10:00 am Monday"] actual: "11:00 pm Sunday. London is 10 hours behind Sydney: 9:00 am − 10 hours goes back past midnight to 11:00 pm the day before." ``` Is London ahead of Sydney or behind? ## Run: one moment, four clocks ```step stage: run insight: "Moving one city's time and watching the others shows the fixed differences and the day changing at midnight." try: { playground: board, starter: "zones.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Was your prediction right? Now set Sydney to 14:00. What time is it in London?", when: "t = 14", explain: "14:00 in Sydney is 04:00 Monday in London: 10 hours behind." } ``` The slider sets Sydney's time; the other cities follow. ## Investigate: ahead and behind ```step stage: investigate insight: "Find the difference of the offsets and its direction (Kim adds for a place behind); the day changes at midnight; 24-hour time removes am and pm slips." tasks: - check: type: number q: "It is 14:00 in Sydney (UTC+11). What hour is it in Perth (UTC+8), in 24-hour time?" answer: 11 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["17", "Perth's offset is smaller: it is behind, so take 3 hours away."] explain: "Perth is 11 − 8 = 3 hours behind: 14:00 − 3 = 11:00." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#kim" text: "Kim finds the time in London. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: tz-wrong-direction explain: "Line 2: London's offset (+1) is smaller than Sydney's (+11), so London is behind: take 10 hours away. 9:00 am Monday becomes 11:00 pm Sunday." - check: type: question q: "Why do flight times use 24-hour time?" options: ["21:30 cannot be mixed up with 9:30 in the morning", "It is shorter to write", "Airports are open 24 hours", "It changes the time zone"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Not the reason.", "Not the reason.", "The zone does not change."] explain: "With 12-hour time, a missing am or pm causes 12-hour mistakes." ``` ### Perth Here is the routine. ```worked +11 - (+1) = 10 :: The difference between the offsets: 10 hours. \text{London's offset is smaller} :: So London is behind Sydney. 09{:}00 - 10\ \text{h} = 23{:}00\ \text{the day before} :: Take it away, crossing midnight back to Sunday. ``` Now find Perth's time. ### Find the mistake Read Kim's working. Is London ahead of Sydney or behind? ### 24-hour time ## Modify: going the other way, and flights ```step stage: modify insight: "Converting into the starting city, a flight across the date line, a working-hours overlap and a target time in another city." try: { playground: board, starter: "zones.yml#run", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "zones.yml#run" hint: ["Sydney is 10 hours ahead of London.", "9:00 + 10 hours."] check: { type: board, text: "It is 9:00 am Monday in London. Set Sydney's time to match.", when: "v = 9 and y = 0", explain: "Sydney is 10 hours ahead: 19:00 (7:00 pm) Monday." } - starter: "zones.yml#flight" hint: ["Add the 14 hours on Sydney's clock first.", "Then take away the 18 hours between Sydney and Los Angeles."] check: type: number q: "A flight leaves Sydney at 22:00 on Friday and takes 14 hours. At what hour (24-hour time) does it land in Los Angeles (UTC−7)? Work it out, then check on the board." answer: 18 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["12", "That is the landing time on Sydney's clock. Los Angeles is 18 hours behind."] explain: "22:00 + 14 h = 12:00 Saturday in Sydney; Los Angeles is 18 hours behind: 18:00 Friday. It lands before it left, by the clock." - check: type: question q: "An office in Sydney works 9:00 to 17:00, and one in London (10 hours behind) works 9:00 to 17:00 their time. Is there an hour when both are at work?" options: ["No: when Sydney starts at 9:00, it is 23:00 in London; when London starts, Sydney has gone home", "Yes: 9:00 to 17:00 in both", "Yes: 12:00 to 13:00", "Only on Mondays"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Their 9:00 is not the same moment.", "Noon in Sydney is 2:00 am in London.", "The days do not matter here."] explain: "Sydney's working day is London's 23:00 to 07:00: no overlap. A meeting needs someone to start early or stay late." - starter: "zones.yml#run" hint: ["Perth is 3 hours behind Sydney.", "Perth's 9:00 is Sydney's 12:00."] check: { type: board, text: "Plan a call between Sydney and Perth that is between 9:00 and 17:00 in both cities. Set Sydney's time, then write the time in both.", when: "t >= 12 and t <= 17", explain: "Perth is 3 hours behind, so Sydney's 12:00 to 17:00 is Perth's 9:00 to 14:00." } ``` ### London to Sydney ### A flight ### Two offices ### Plan a call ## Practise: time zones ```step stage: practise insight: "Conversions both ways, a duration, and 12- and 24-hour time, mixed; adding for a place behind is the planted slip; durations in one zone come first." tasks: - check: type: number q: "It is 10:00 in Sydney (UTC+11). What hour is it in Perth (UTC+8), in 24-hour time?" answer: 7 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["13", "Perth's offset is smaller: it is behind. Take 3 hours away."] explain: "Perth is 3 hours behind: 10:00 − 3 = 07:00." smaller: check: { type: question, q: "Sydney is UTC+11 and Perth is UTC+8. Is Perth's clock earlier or later than Sydney's?", options: ["Earlier", "Later"], answer: 0, explain: "Perth's offset is 3 less, so it is 3 hours earlier. Its time is Sydney's time with 3 hours taken off." } - check: type: number q: "A train leaves at 08:45 and arrives at 17:20 the same day (one time zone). How many minutes is the trip?" answer: 515 tolerance: 0 explain: "08:45 to 17:00 is 8 h 15 min; plus 20 min is 8 h 35 min = 515 minutes." - check: type: question q: "What is 21:45 in 12-hour time?" options: ["9:45 pm", "9:45 am", "10:45 pm", "11:45 pm"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "After 12:00 it is pm.", "21 − 12 = 9, not 10.", "21 − 12 = 9."] explain: "21 − 12 = 9: 9:45 pm." - check: type: number q: "It is 23:00 on Sunday in Perth (UTC+8). What hour is it in Sydney (UTC+11), in 24-hour time? (It is Monday there.)" answer: 2 tolerance: 0 explain: "23:00 + 3 hours = 02:00 on Monday." - check: type: number q: "A flight leaves Perth at 06:00 Perth time and lands in Sydney at 13:00 Sydney time. How many hours is the flight?" answer: 4 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["7", "The two times are on different clocks. 06:00 in Perth is 09:00 in Sydney."] explain: "06:00 in Perth is 09:00 in Sydney; 09:00 to 13:00 is 4 hours." ``` ### Sydney to Perth ### A trip's length ### 12-hour time ### Past midnight ### A flight's length ## Make: plan an arrival ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing a departure so an arrival lands in a window brings the offset, the flight and the day together." try: { playground: board, starter: "zones.yml#plan", height: 600 } hint: ["The flight is 14 hours and Los Angeles is 18 hours behind Sydney.", "Arrival (LA time) = departure + 14 − 18 = departure − 4."] check: { type: board, text: "A 14-hour flight leaves Sydney on Saturday. Choose a departure time so it lands in Los Angeles between 9:00 and 12:00 local time.", when: "a >= 9 and a <= 12", explain: "Departure − 4 hours is the landing time: leave between 13:00 and 16:00." } ``` Then write both times for your flight, in 24-hour time with the day, as you would on a ticket. ## Make: the final, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Overseas sport is the offset difference, the direction, and the day: Sydney is ahead of London, so add, and cross midnight into the next day." hint: ["Which offset is bigger?", "Add the difference, and if you pass 24:00, take 24 away and move to the next day."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A made-up final kicks off at 8 pm (20:00) on Saturday 17 October 2026, London time (UTC+1 on that date). It is shown live in Sydney (UTC+11). At what hour, in 24-hour time, does it start in Sydney? Say which day it is there, too." steps: - ["Sydney is $11 - 1 = 10$ hours ahead of London", "the bigger offset is ahead"] - ["$20{:}00 + 10\\ \\text{h} = 30{:}00$", "ahead means add"] - ["$30{:}00 - 24 = 06{:}00$, on Sunday 18 October", "past midnight is the next day"] picks: - step: 1 q: "How do you decide which way to go?" options: - "Sydney's offset (+11) is bigger than London's (+1), so Sydney is ahead: add 10 hours" - "Sydney is behind London, so take 10 hours away" - "Add 11 hours, Sydney's whole offset" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The bigger offset is ahead, and +11 is bigger than +1.", "London is already +1, so the difference is 10, not 11."] answer: "6" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["10", "That takes the 10 hours away. Sydney is ahead, so add them and cross midnight."] - ["30", "30:00 is past midnight. Take away 24 to get the hour on the next day."] - ["7", "That adds 11, the whole of Sydney's offset. London is already +1, so add the difference, 10."] criteria: - "I compared the two offsets and said which city is ahead." - "I changed the day when I passed midnight." - "I wrote the time in 24-hour time." explain: "Sydney is 11 − 1 = 10 hours ahead of London. 20:00 + 10 h = 30:00, which is 06:00 on Sunday 18 October in Sydney." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The final is made up for the task, and the answer uses the offsets for 4 to 24 October 2026, so it holds only on a date in that window. Write the offsets, the sum and the day, then type the hour. **Also used in** - **Watching sport live.** A match overseas kicks off at a strange hour here. Daylight saving moves different places' clocks on different dates, so the gap can change by an hour. - **Calls to family abroad.** Work out whose clock is later before you ring, or you wake someone up. - **Flights.** A flight's arrival time is local time at the landing city, so it can look earlier than the departure. ```teacher summary: Students move one city's time and watch the others follow, convert between time zones using UTC offsets, and plan flights and a call across zones (AC9M8M04, nodes 1 and 2). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can change a time from one time zone to another using UTC offsets. - I can tell when the day changes. - I can work out when a flight lands, in local time. struggle: Ahead or behind. Ask students to compare the two offsets and say whose clock is later before they add or take away. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. The one idea: the city with the bigger offset is ahead; find the difference, add or take it away, and change the day at midnight. The common mistake is adding when the other city is behind (Kim's mistake). The offsets in this lesson hold from 4 October to 25 October 2026: Sydney UTC+11 (daylight saving, from 4 October; +10 before), Perth +8, Tokyo +9, London +1 (British Summer Time ends 25 October), Los Angeles −7 (until 1 November). Go by offsets, not east and west on a map: Los Angeles is east of Sydney but behind, across the date line. Daylight saving changes them through the year, and not every Australian state uses it; check current offsets for real planning. Wider: the International Date Line, why some zones are offset by half an hour (Adelaide, India), and planning a fair regular meeting for staff in several states and another country. running: - "Predict: ask which offset is bigger." - "Run: ask what happens to London's day as Sydney's time moves." - "Investigate: ask Kim to check her answer on the board." - "Modify: ask how a flight can land before it took off." - "Make: ask for the times as they would appear on a ticket." - "Paper: the overseas final is worked in books. Books out; look for the direction decided from the offsets before any adding, and the day written down. The answer holds only for dates from 4 to 24 October 2026." stuck: - see: A student adds the difference for a city that is behind. ask: Which offset is bigger? Which clock is later? fix: "Bigger offset: ahead (add). Smaller: behind (take away)." - see: A student gets the right hour but the wrong day. ask: Did you cross midnight? fix: Going past 24:00 is the next day; going below 00:00 is the day before. - see: A student adds the flight time but does not change to the arrival zone. ask: Whose clock is your answer on? fix: Add the flight on the departure clock, then change to the arrival zone (or change first, then add). stretch: Plan a video call between Sydney, Perth and London that falls between 8:00 and 21:00 for everyone. Is there one? Which city has to compromise most? support: A printed strip of 24-hour lines for each city, to slide against each other. leads: > This completes AC9M8M04. Where it leads: rates such as speed and time (Rates), and planning tasks in other subjects (Geography's time zones and the date line). exit: q: It is 18:30 Tuesday in Sydney (UTC+11). What time and day is it in Los Angeles (UTC−7)? a: "Los Angeles is 18 hours behind: 00:30 Tuesday." explain: > A **time zone** is an offset from UTC. A city with a bigger offset is **ahead**; a smaller one is **behind**. Find the difference, add or take it away, and change the **day** when you cross midnight. For a flight, add the flight time to the departure (in the departure zone), then change to the arrival zone. Use **24-hour time** to avoid am and pm mistakes. sources: - title: "Daylight saving in NSW: starts 4 October 2026, ends 4 April 2027 (NSW Government)" url: https://www.nsw.gov.au/about-nsw/daylight-saving checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "When do the clocks change: back on 25 October 2026 (GOV.UK)" url: https://www.gov.uk/when-do-the-clocks-change checked: 2026-10-12 - title: "Los Angeles clock changes: daylight saving ends 1 November 2026 (timeanddate.com)" url: https://www.timeanddate.com/time/change/usa/los-angeles checked: 2026-10-12 ```
